text:
The plethora of raytracing injection videos on youtube are hosted by people who think screen space reflections at the default of 1 are the cats meow. Nevermind that EVERYTHING is mirrorlike, this reflective layer alone (Like Ambient occlussion) when set waaaaaay too high bleeds through effects like smoke, fog, and water filters. They also dont scale back the added overall color in the scene from injection bouncing colors around from the light spectrum, and texture to texture, and like the reshade calibrationists think that changing the color intensity of the artists intention in the shaders, either think they can do it better, or have very little sentience to their lack of respect for higher art. My philosophy is preserve the assets as the artists intended them, and to make them clearer. Raytracing however adds layers of rendering that were not previously possible the artists would likely have used themselves. The trick is subtlety because going too far, breaks renders at specific points in the game.

Its a matter of time until their everything must be mirrorified becomes a meme with the coming popularization of raytracing meets retro, I will serve in my own way, as the cultural spearhead.
author: @remasteredretropcgames3312

text:
Oh and Sir Linus, Quincunx vs FXAA is a very comparable algorithm IQ wise. FXAA being a hair less blurring, albeit very computationally efficient. Why did one go extinct requiring nvinspector and old code paths like AVP2 has, but FXAA didnt? Im digging the mass grave, and you can be the machine gun pit crew for the 0 to 1 complex that refuses death. The company nvidia needs to step far away from this necromancy. Getting the community awareness turnt up to 11 is the momentum needed. 

Depth + color based SMAA curbstomps it in image quality. The minor almost non existent texture blur at awkward angles despite antistrophic filtering are controlled by intelligent sharpening. Remember how trashy dumb sharpeners were for years? Ive found one that doesnt look awful, and it works on nvidia cards despite being open sourced by AMD. 

You should do Gods work, and long after this comment is forgotten, urge FXAA's abandonment and ultimate replacement with the more modern, objectively superior algorithm. Literally you have major development teams that are using it because its just kind of there to use. Crowbar collectives members arent the lone rangers. Im particularly annoyed with metro exodus' development team shrugging and sort of releasing a console port so half heartedly. Id love to turn off the in game retardation based sharpener, even if I can get around their version of FXAA without breaking light rendering with DLSS. I of course lack the tier card to do so at this time but its still a stupid decision I see more often than I should mostly because its obvious they arent autistically focused on the minutia, despite it being the honest to God lens we see their entire world through.

I've bought a prebuild Lenovo Legion 5T (w/ Ryzen 7 5800) and this 3060ti for 950 Euro. I was looking at a prebuild with this GPU specifically since my max budget was 1000 Euro, and the Lenovo was the only one currently sitting at 950! (The other prebuilds (MSI/HP OMEN/Victus etc.) with 3060ti were all priced above 1200 Euro or came with the newer 3070's). The same system with a 3070 was 1349 Euro (w/ discount) and well above my budget. I even tried to pick the same components as the prebuild for a DIY build and couldn't get the price below 1250 Euro, so the prebuild was a no-brainer.

I was so lucky with my purchase price because only two days after my purchase (end of May 2023), the price of my prebuild system went up to 1449 Euro, where it still sits currenty as of this writing.

I think 950 Euro for a R7 5800/3060ti/16GB DDR4 is a steal, since the 3060ti stand-alone still cost around 300-350 Euro even on the secondhand market. And i have to say this card is a beast!

text: What's the diff in performance for cards from diff manufacturers? I have a prebuilt coming with a 3060Ti and even though I knew the likely answer I asked them who would make the card in my build, and they said whichever card we have
author: @seekthe9

text:
@seekthe9  some manufacturers will overclock their chips and put extra cooling on there to boost performance a bit. But a 3060 Ti from any manufacturer will perform within a few percent of a 3060 Ti from any other manufacturer. It’s all a matter of degrees. 

Even two 3060 Ti reference cards directly from nVidia can differ by a bit - each individual chip’s quality can vary a tiny amount.  It’s all just the luck of the draw.

My 3060ti is weird, it's a FE model but the cooler is odd .. when trying to overclock the card I noticed anything above about 50% fan speed does absolutely nothing. I can have the card at 2130mhz and 50% fan speed 67c I could crank the fan speed to 100% it might drop to 65c but it is more or less the same. The card doesn't run any cooler above 50% fan speed, of course if I have it at desktop and crank the fans than yes the temp will be under 65c but while under any load 51-100% fan speed = 65c 

Makes no sense to me, my old 980ti would drop a good 10c, same story for my 7970 before that .. this is the first card I've owned which the cooler works fine, but any fan speed over 50% does absolutely nothing. The card functions, and the cooler does work, it doesn't overheat, so I don't think its bad contact, or a bad thermal paste application from the factory but it still makes absolutely no sense to me....

text: @PatrickRatman  and btw have you ever watched any YouTube videos about ibuypower PCs? They are always horribly built and they choose the cheapest parts possible just so they can mark up the price and pretend they have top of the line equipment. May I ask, how is the cable management? What power supply did it come with? What cooler did it come with? Dual channel ram? What motherboard did it come with?
author: @smirky2639

text:
@smirky2639  First of all, i didn't buy it hoping for excellent cable management and top of the line equipment, and didn't care about dual channel ram. I bought it knowing that if i tried to build the PC myself with the exact same parts at this moment in time i would be paying more because GPUs are being sold at a disgusting 200-300% markup right now, and i didn't want to camp out at freaking microcenter at 6 in the morning hoping to win the GPU lottery. i don't need your lecture about the superiority of dual channel ram or why you think my power supply is going to explode. I just wanted a gaming pc and i wanted it quick, and i was willing to jump through some hoops to make sure it worked properly, and it was the only prebuilt at the moment that had a RTX 30 series in it that wasn't out of stock.

MB is Asus Prime Z490-P
ram is teamgroup t-force delta DDR4 RGB 3200mHz 16gb. i bought another pair cause i play DCS: World which usually needs 32gb ram for high intensity missions, and even though it's probably mediocre RGB "coolgamer" kind of RAM it gets the job done and the sim loads in less than 10 seconds with no stuttering. 
the CPU cooler is one of IBP's own 240mm liquid coolers, but seems to do the job when i test the temps on GPUZ. one of the parts i'll probably have to keep an eye on and probably replace myself with something better later down the line if they haven't managed to fix the problems i've heard, but not a life ending problem if i need to as i have a job and i don't expect to be poor in a few months when the problems typically crop up.
Power supply is the only one i expected to be iffy, as it's listed as a "650 Watt - HIGH POWER 80 PLUS Gold" with no particular brand name listed, so i can only assume it's a knockoff that comes from china. i've been reading that one on GPUZ as well and it doesn't seem like it's going to explode any time soon, but i'll probably be replacing it when i get the chance just to be safe.
video card is a MSI RTX 3060ti Gaming X trio and CPU is a i7 10700kf 8 core.

When i got it, i updated the bios, switched XMP on and MCE off in the advanced settings in the bios as advised by Gamer's Nexus as their ibuypower VS Wal-Mart PC review covered on from about two years ago and its been running fine. cable management is a bit messy but not awful. was able to install a Samsung 870 QVO 2tb SSD pretty cleanly and screwed into the PSU shroud, tho i had to unplug the HDD's sata cable to getthe magnetic shroud mount out properly cause of the spacing. most of the cables plugged into the MB (mostly for RGB shite) are routed through the case holes to the appropriate pin headers in a way that my basic bish brain probably wouldn't have done any better myself.

text:
Linus, I am a huge fan and I am grateful for a lot of your content. But your disclaimer before your conclusion is either using backwards logic or entirely disingenuous. You say that even though you know that the 3060 Ti's actual current price is vastly higher than its theoretical price, it's still okay to judge the card by the latter price right now because this video is going to be online forever. So as the two price values eventually meet, whenever the hell that is, your review will become more and more accurate.

1. This video will be online forever, yes, but the value proposition of electronics declines steeply and quickly. You know this. Everyone knows this. When the 4060 Ti or whatever equivalent card launches in 2023 for $399 or less, do you think this review will still be relevant with regards to informing value-oriented consumers of what to buy? In short, the fact that this video will be around forever doesn't make it relevant forever.

2. Do you go back to your older videos and re-edit them to inform anyone who might be watching them now and in the future of price drops (or even increases)? For example, your beloved Note 9 is an incredible value at its price today compared to its price when it was released. So do you do that? If you don't, then you can't apply that same logic to these reviews of scarce and scalped products.

3. You cannot be part of the hype machine while condemning the opportunists who are taking advantage of the hype you generated. Choose one. Either you take the high ground and release this review and praise this ONLY WHEN IT'S ACTUALLY WIDELY AVAILABLE AT ITS MSRP, or you have some self-awareness and accountability and admit that flooding YouTube with praise about these scarce products at launch time is HELPING SCALPERS. You are one of the biggest, if not the biggest tech reviewers today, and yet even you can't manage to delay your reviews to dampen the hype. Hell, you use the same face reaction thumbnail as everyone else. 

There is nothing inherently wrong with doing whatever legitimate trick it takes to make money. Releasing reviews for products that are barely available? Sure, go ahead. Clickbait YouTube thumbnails? It's your right. What is wrong is either this hypocrisy or complete lack of self-awareness, pretending that you are not part of the machine that encourages anti-consumer behavior.

text: He did what he could with what he had.  He was honest that the card was defective which if anything tells us that NVIDIA didn't hand pick the cards to make sure they were good or better than average.  Given that he could still review most of the cards stats it made perfect sense for him to do it this way.  Also consider what would have happened if he either didn't put out a video or put out a short one that just said his review card was defective.  In the former case he'd get heat for not doing a review at all and could easily lose some viewership (the algorithm is a harsh mistress).  In the latter case it would have been disingenuous to NVIDIA since they could still review most aspects of the card and the results were pretty good, if he just ended the video with 'card was defective' then people may instead think they are all bad (even though logically it doesn't make sense to judge every card based on one bad experience that's how people tend to be).  Once they can get a new non-defective card I'm sure they update their review as necessary.

text:
I'll be honest - you SHOULD report the MRSP price. Look, that's the price the retailers are supposed to sell it at *or less*. Nvidia has consistently underestimated demand for these cards and have taken no reasonable steps to limit scalpers - so they're part of the problem. Scalpers aren't retailers in the normal sense and aren't bound by agreements with Nvidia, so they're free to sell at whatever price they can get away with. How do YOU report on this? More importantly - reporting on their prices legitimizes their pricing.

Reporting on the scalper prices relative to MRSP could help by underlining the problem, but LTT isn't the cause of it - Nvidia and all the computer stores who just want to dump as many cards as they can to make the max profit as fast as possible are. I'm not even going to blame scalpers - that's how capitalism and the rule of supply and demand works. But we went through this big time when bitcoin miners basically wiped out everyone's GPU stock. We went through it with the 3070 and 3080. Nvidia doesn't seem to learn... clearly doesn't care enough about their customers to fix this problem.

It's not your problem. And people who are yelling at you? They're entitled Karens who need to vent their anger at the right people. And get a life.

Cheers.

text:
Linus. Back off bro. You're shilling. At 2:26 it didn't 'nearly match' the 6800 in SOTR, unless you're prepared to say it 'nearly matched' the 3070, as the 6800 and 3070 were only 1fps apart in your own testing. 

2:30 Yes. all of the RTX cards beat the AMD cards in RTX Minecraft because it was written for nVidia's RTX api. This should also hold true for RTX Quake. While this is still a valid point, it would be more meaningful if RTX MC was written in the DX ray tracing API.

2:40 You don't even explain the lack of a score for the 6800?

2:45 Let's just gloss over that.... no mention at all

3:00 It 'nearly beats out' the 2080 TI? Are you kidding? It's on par with the 2080 TI. None of it's scores are actually higher, but if we consider driver issues and 'margin of error' you could legitimately consider them equals, though both score lower than the 6800, 3070, and 3080. In fact you could say that, based on the graph, the 3060 and the 2080 TI were tied for second to last place.

3:20 Ok. The 3070 does well on Blender. Nicely done. But the issue here is that a Venn Diagram of 'those who game inexpensively' and 'those who use Blender on a regular basis' have a very small overlap.

3:28 Lets overlook that no explanation is given for 'no score' for the 6800 for several tests. Yes, many viewers may understand why this is, but you should spell it out for those who don't.

3:47  No. The 3060 isn't 'trading blows' with the 2080 TI. The 2080 TI out scores it in all three benchmarks handily. In fact, it ties two out of three benchmarks with the 2080 Super and while it beats the 2080 Super in the third, it's still well short of the 2080 TI. Again, the 3060 is second to last.

3:50 The 3060 is last place. The 2080 TI beats it on every score and the 2080 Super beats it or ties it on two of three scores. This is especially important as the 3080 is a newer gen.

 3:54 the 3060 loses to the 2080 Ti and only beats the 2080 Super on one score, though all solidly beat the 6800. So whether it 'wins' or not is based completely on your metric. I need to say again that synthetic benchmarks for apps that likely won't be used on the card in question are of dubious value at best. If you're looking at a 'budget constrained gamer', then the 3060 is a clear winner. If you're using tools like Maya, Blender, and/or Solidworks, you're probably going to buy a different card to begin with - the 3060 isn't even on your radar, so such benchmarks are relatively pointless.

Now if you can get it at MSRP, this is a decent card, but only if you can get it at MSRP. If you're rockin a 2080 Super or better, leave your cash in your wallet - this isn't for you. You'll see almost no performance increase. Yes, some games will do better, some will do worse. But if you're going to shell out a minimum of $400, everything should run faster.

Hell, If you already have a 20xx card, I wouldn't upgrade at all until the 3080 comes down to MSRP and I'd only upgrade then if you're dead set on getting a better card. If you have a 10xx card and you want to stick with an NVIDIA GPU, this is a great option once the price stabilizes.

Linus, I'm disappointed in you. From a disinterested point of view (not team red or green) you really came across as being paid to shine a spotlight on this card.

[edit]
The best sales pitch would be that with the 3060, you get performance that lands between the 2080 Super and the 2080 TI for "just" $400.

Do keep in mind "MSRP" usually does not include the VAT (Value Added Tax) or any other extra-costs
( E.G. import and other customs-fees ).
Hence why it is indeed only called "manufacturer's suggested retail price" for the item itself/alone;
the ( genuine non-scalping ) resellers still gotta make some net-profit after all the additional costs to get their hands into these plus all the other post-sale expenses.
---

text: @PaveMentman  The MSRP in Germany always includes VAT. 3060Ti FE MSRP is €399. Also, MSRP does include import. The cards are produced in Taiwan, the RETAIL price is including all costs, it's not the manufacturing cost but the eventual retail price.

text:
I love the point on the pricing. Scalper pricing doesn't have a base. It's just... "haha, offer and demand, F u, you can't buy it anywhere else so it's my way or the highway". MSRP exists as a way to segment the market, which is a positive because it makes sure authorized resellers don't do this and jack up pricing.
Besides it's just a move to prey on early buyers who have no patience. While it sucks that you can't buy the new GPU for the price it was designed to be bought for... you can wait. In the end, waiting on the scalpers makes them waste time and money because they don't get a profit off the money they spent in the first place, and if they sell it at the MSRP a few months down the line, they spent all their time and effort for nothing, and might even be at a loss considering it costs money to warehouse things, for "large" scalpers like the assholes who bought the 3000+ PS5s. 
So just wait them out. If there is no profit to be had, they won't be able to do this in the long run

text: The MSRP being wrong is not a new thing, 20 series cards had the same problem. It's difficult, because manufacturer's can't control the pricing of all of their vendors. But in this situation where the cards are simply unavailable at MSRP, you are right to highlight this. The principle of price skimming suggests MSRP should be the base price (set at a point where supply meets anticipated demand, or a point slightly above), and over time as demand drops the price is supposed to drop to entice further customers. Over the past few years it seems every card released has its price elevated for months before dropping down to MSRP only when on special offers and such. I'm not sure the RTX 2070 super for example ever dropped to MSRP and it's incredibly frustrating for consumers when we're looking for the best bang for buck, and all the reviews give the misleading info provided by the manufacturer. It makes them appear a better value proposition than they actually are, or ever will be. It needs more than a caveat, you should straight up say the MSRP is not applicable and should be ignored.

text:
That's the reason I didn't bother upgrading to Turing from my 1080Ti. The 2080 performed similar for the same price in rasterization and there were no titles supporting real time ray tracing.

This kind of technology will be outdated by next gen. When the successor of Ampère releases the 30 series cards will be outdated and the real time ray tracing performance will be borderline unusable or at its lowest setting. If you want real time ray tracing working on the current games of which Watchdogs Legion is the best example (because it doesn't need an ultra high refresh rate) then go ahead and buy a 30 series card (once it's available) but don't expect to future proof your rig because you're doing the exact opposite. So if you want to play Cyberpunk and your GPU is still fine for everything else you play, just wait until it actually releases (you never know) and then judge if the difference of real time ray tracing is worth it to you. If you don't expect to play Cyberpunk or any other current/about to be released ray tracing title then you might as well get the slightly extra rasterization performance RDNA2 provides.

The previous paragraph aren't my words (although I totally agree with them) but the words of Hardware Unboxed. And you with a 20 series card know it's true. I'm personally expecting to buy a 3080Ti (a couple months after it releases in January🤣) just because I want real time ray tracing in Watchdogs but I also expect to replace it in 2-3 years (depending on generational improvements) so it isn't a big deal to me when the old card starts falling short. But if I would expect to keep the graphics card longer I'd buy a 6900XT because it will most likely provide better rasterization performance.

Mark my words, there will come a time where games will require ray tracing and games may look like shit without it.

I could be wrong, but in my opinion RT isnt going away like it's some kind of phase. It's a better process of development. As of now, game developers are actually taking the time to do both, but this wont just go away like bell bottom Jeans.
author: @Xehemoth

text: @Xehemoth  Your raytracing isn't going away but the performance will be insignificant in 2 generations so it will be almost unusable (or at least very outdated) anyway. By which time you either have to stick to minimum settings @ 27fps, upgrade or just use rasterization. For game developers the real time raytracing performance is now potato like for what they actually want to create. Only Minecraft and Quake at this moment can use its full potential but anything with higher graphical fidelity can't be fully ray traced anyway (Tomb Raider only ray traces shadows, not reflections for example). So game developers will keep implementing shadows and reflections the old fashioned way until everything can be ray traced. Developers will keep implementing it more and more with each generation though so older generations will lag behind very quickly on high settings. Best you can hope for on your old cards is console like performance and graphical fidelity which doesn't sound that bad right now but it will in 2 years. But if you have to turn real time raytracing off you might as well make use of more rasterization performance. A 2080Ti ffs can't even run Watchdogs Legion at a decent framerate 30+fps with real time raytracing on a high setting right now and that's "only" a last gen flagship that had dedicated hardware for it. The same will happen with the 30series (especially if Nvidia wants to stay ahead of AMD somewhere).

@malcolmfenech1749  false, these scalpers exist by exploiting tools to give them advantage over a typical consumer. At the end of the day it’s the retail companies fault for not putting more protections in place. They have no legal obligation to do so but from an ethical and free market standpoint they are responsible for maintaining the integrity of their sales system. 
This can be done but prohibiting bots or creating their wide availability so that one consumer doesn’t have an advantage over another. The retail companies are acting unethically however b/c they are given no incentive to do so beyond creating goodwill with their consumer. They have likely come to the conclusion that consumers have short memories and this is a temporary situation so they’re going to collect their profits first and worry about the fallout later. Long story short, bots are immoral as long as they are not widely available. The brick and mortar equivalent of this is placing a store on the top of a mountain and notifying users to take the long path to get there all the while providing a back door to the short path and turning a blind eye. Structural exploitation is legal but definitely immoral and you should get mad at retail companies for not standing up for the avg consumer. Best way to do that is to not give them your money and let them know why you chose to go else where. I.e buying direct from manufacturer via something like EVGA queue system.

text:
On the whole, I think I can do without any more videos discussing phantom products the the average consumer has no chance of owning until heaven knows when.  I understand that reporting this kind of news is your business, but I am coming to the conclusion, unfortunately, that this kind of coverage is part of the problem.  Every YouTube influencer that produces one of these videos continues to reward the manufacturers for NOT getting their product to market efficiently by creating pent-up demand that does not diminish when those same manufacturers continue to FAIL to meet that demand.  

I would much prefer it if you and other channels would adopt a policy of not using any product in your videos that you DID NOT OBTAIN THROUGH NORMAL RETAIL CHANNELS.  This would ensure that manufacturers can only enjoy the promotion of their products WHEN THEY ARE ABLE TO DELIVERY THEM.  I know that's unrealistic but until that happens, I fear there will be little incentive for them to improve their performance.  So until then, I think I will stop watching these videos.  Including this one.  Sorry, Linus, it's not much, but it's all I can do to address the issue. I will not watch any more videos for products I cannot buy.

text:
Meh, got nothing against the scalpers. Its Nvidias fault that its not in stock and only their fault. Had they charged twice as much money, this wouldnt be happening. Now, maybe that wouldve been to much, but fact is, the market price is far greater than what they charge, that will in a perfect economy lead to a shadow market where it costs around the market value PLUS the difference between what they charge and the market value.
Say they charge 500$ and it would otherwise normaly be worth around 750$ if thats what they were charging, then itll be going for 1000$. We call this a deadweight loss in economics. And, yes, that works in the opposite case, too, when itss priced higher than market value, hence cigarette smuggling is a thing.

text: Look at the 95th percentile min. It's a much more meaningful number. AMD has a history of making cards that have high average FPS to look good on tests, but FPS which fluctuates wildly. The 95th percentile shows the minimum framerate you can expect to get 95% of the time. 5% might not seem like a lot, but jumps in performance, even if they are rare, can be just as if not more jarring and unpleasant than low but consistent performance. Plus, even if you look at the average, 7fps for 300 dollars isn't exactly a killer lead.

text:
Dodging again where the blame really lies, namely *buyers*. Using the word 'scalpers' is not an argument, it ignores that the only reason why such a phenomena exists for any product is because other people are willing to buy them, and every purchase is a voluntary transaction. It wouldn't be an issue if retailers were allowed to set whatever pricing they saw fit based on demand levels vs. supply (which NVIDIA et al don't allow), but the tech media has a bee in its bonnet over that idea because most people don't understand how supply & demand works. The only difference is both NVIDIA and AMD are exploiting the market distortions to maximise their margins, which does kinda suck, but at the end of the day it's not their fault if buyers are unable to defer gratification. Too many people seem incapable of resisting the hype and just spend, often using credit.

https://libertarianinstitute.org/articles/why-price-gouging-actually-helps-during-a-crisis/

The free market can be excellently self correcting, but only if it's allowed to be; the ignorant will observe what's going on atm with GPU/CPU supply and blame capitalism, which is even dumber when the market isn't operating freely and is being manipulated with dishonest intent.

Well, to anyone wondering, I have:
R5 2600
16GB 3000MHz RAM
1TB NVMe
500W PSU

Paired with a 1050ti and 2x 1080p75Hz monitors. Altogether I'm very happy with it. The only thing that I feel is lacking, is the power of my GPU, with 4GB VRAM, a lot of games have to downgrade their textures to fit in. The lack of raw power behind the GPU, with 768 Cuda Cores, is only supported by an OC to 1980MHz. It won't go any higher because the 1050ti is limited by a 75W PCIe-slot power budget. Still chuggs along in modern titles though, even after 4 years.
